title: AI in Hiring Process
text:
The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to review and write resumes raises concerns about how it affects creativity, critical thinking, and a reviewer’s ability to recognize a candidate’s true qualifications. Many job applicants now use AI tools to improve grammar, organize information, and tailor resumes to job descriptions. At the same time, employers and hiring managers are also using AI systems to screen and evaluate applications more quickly. While these technologies can make hiring more efficient, they also raise important ethical concerns. One concern is how the use of AI may affect an applicant’s creativity and critical thinking skills. When AI generates resume content, it may reduce the need for individuals to reflect on their own experiences and communicate them in their own voice. Another concern is whether hiring managers can accurately recognize a candidate’s true qualifications when resumes are heavily assisted by AI. If many applicants use similar AI tools, resumes may begin to look alike, making it harder to distinguish genuine skills and experiences. For example, some companies have already reported an increase in AI-generated resumes, making it harder to distinguish between candidates and evaluate authentic qualifications. Overall, the growing use of AI in resume writing and review raises questions about fairness, transparency, and trust in the hiring process. This leads to the central question of this case:
Is it fair to use AI to write resumes in the hiring process?

title: Impacts
text:
Descriptions of stakeholders (from Worksheet):
Job Applicants Job applicants are individuals who submit resumes when applying for jobs. Some applicants use AI tools to help write or improve their resumes, while others do not.
Impact - Applicants with access to AI tools may gain an advantage, while those without access may be rejected more often, even if equally qualified. - Increased competition may pressure all applicants to use AI tools, even if they prefer not to. Interests - Fair evaluation of qualifications - Equal opportunity in hiring - Transparency in hiring decisions
Other Relevant Information - Applicants may have different levels of access to technology and different levels of experience using AI tools.
Resume Reviewers Resume reviewers are individuals responsible for reading and evaluating resumes during the hiring process.
Impact: - They may rely too heavily on AI tools, potentially overlooking strong candidates who do not match AI-generated patterns. - Their role may change or become reduced as automation increases.
Interests: Efficient review of applications Accurate identification of qualified candidates Reduced workload
Other Relevant Information Their decisions directly affect which candidates move forward in the hiring process.
Human Resources (HR) HR professionals manage hiring processes and ensure that companies follow hiring policies and employment laws.
Impact - They must balance efficiency with fairness while ensuring AI tools do not introduce discrimination. - They may face challenges in regulating and monitoring AI use.
Interests Fair and legal hiring practices Efficient hiring processes Reliable evaluation methods
Other Relevant Information HR departments are responsible for balancing efficiency with ethical responsibility.
AI Companies AI companies develop the tools used to generate and evaluate resumes.
Impact - They benefit financially from increased AI use but are responsible for ensuring fairness and accuracy. - Poorly designed systems could contribute to bias in hiring.
Interests Innovation and product development User trust Responsible technology use
Other Relevant Information The design of AI systems can influence hiring outcomes.
The Environment The environment represents natural resources affected by the operation of AI technology and data centers.
Impact Increased use of AI contributes to higher energy and water consumption, which may negatively impact the environment over time
Interests Sustainable technology development Reduced resource consumption
Other Relevant Information Environmental impact is a long-term concern as AI use continues to grow.

title: Ethical Issues
text: Ethical issues: The use of AI to write resumes raises concerns about fairness in hiring. Applicants who use AI tools may have an advantage over those who do not. For example, some applicants use AI as a shortcut to adjust their base resume to the job they are applying to. Another way that some use AI to their advantage is by adding keywords that they know the AI will identify as qualified. Employers may also struggle to determine whether resumes accurately represent a candidate’s real skills and experiences. In addition to fairness, this ethical issue also raises concerns about trust, bias, and transparency. Transparency is important because employers may not know how much of a resume was generated by AI. Bias can occur if AI tools favor certain writing styles or backgrounds. Accessibility is a concern because not all applicants have equal access to AI tools. Trust is affected when employers are unsure whether resumes reflect genuine skills.

Discussion Questions:
Is the connection between culture and applicants’ stories seen in applications? How has it changed?
Should employers treat AI-assisted resumes differently from fully human-written resumes? Why or why not?
Does access to AI technology create an unfair advantage for some applicants?
How can companies verify that the skills listed on resumes are genuine?
Should there be limits on how much AI can be used in the hiring process?
